record.paper_title: Advances and Open Problems in Federated Learning
record.original_question: In cross-silo federated learning, especially when participating organizations may also be competitors, how should incentives be designed to reward honest participation, divide value created by the jointly trained model, optimize participation, and connect incentives with defenses against adversarial data owners?

evidence.quote: incentive mechanism design for honest participation

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a cross-silo federated learning setting with a fixed set of N organizations (silos) indexed by i = 1, ..., N. Each silo i holds a private dataset D_i drawn from a local distribution and, by participating, contributes computational effort and data to train a shared global model f_theta with parameters theta in R^d. Let U_i(theta, a_i, a_{-i}) denote the utility silo i derives from the resulting model when it takes action a_i in A_i (an action space encoding choices such as how much data to contribute, the truthfulness of reported gradients, and whether to inject adversarial or poisoned data) and the other silos take actions a_{-i}. Some silos may also be product-market competitors, so U_i may depend negatively on the quality of the model received by other silos.

Design an incentive mechanism M consisting of:
(1) a participation/reward rule r: (a_1, ..., a_N) -> (r_1, ..., r_N) in R^N that allocates the value V(theta) created by the jointly trained model among the silos,
(2) a contribution-elicitation rule that determines what each silo must submit,
(3) a defense/auditing rule connecting payments r_i to detection of adversarial behavior by silo i,

such that the mechanism simultaneously satisfies the following formal requirements:

(a) Honest participation is a (dominant-strategy or Bayes–Nash) equilibrium: for every silo i and every alternative action a_i' in A_i, E[U_i(theta, a_i^*, a_{-i}^*) + r_i] >= E[U_i(theta', a_i', a_{-i}^*) + r_i'], where a_i^* denotes honest participation.

(b) The value-division rule r is budget-balanced (sum_i r_i = V(theta)) and satisfies a fairness axiom such as the Shapley value characterization with respect to the marginal contributions of each silo's data to model performance.

(c) Participation is individually rational and the equilibrium maximizes the total number of silos that choose to participate, subject to (a) and (b).

(d) The mechanism is robust to adversarial data owners: there exists a detection/penalty function so that any silo deviating to an adversarial action a_i' (e.g., data poisoning, backdoor injection, or model-degradation attack designed to harm competitors) receives expected utility strictly less than under honest participation, while honest silos suffer at most epsilon loss in model quality.

Provide such a mechanism, or prove impossibility, in a model that explicitly captures competition between silos (i.e., where each U_i can depend negatively on U_j for j != i through downstream market effects of the shared model).
artifact.status_search_result: Incentive design for cross-silo federated learning with competing organizations remains an active research area. While numerous partial proposals exist (Shapley-value-based reward schemes, contract-theoretic and game-theoretic mechanisms, and various robust aggregation defenses), no mechanism is known that jointly satisfies honest participation, fair value division, optimal participation, and integrated defense against adversarial silos in the competitor setting. The problem is generally regarded as open.

status_evidence.title: Advances and Open Problems in Federated Learning
status_evidence.snippet: Lists incentive mechanism design for honest participation among cross-silo participants as an open problem.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is identified as open in the federated learning literature.

status_evidence.title: A Survey of Incentive Mechanism Design for Federated Learning
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys partial approaches (Shapley-value, contract theory, Stackelberg games) but notes no unified mechanism integrating fairness, participation, and robustness to adversaries.
status_evidence.claim: Existing approaches are partial; the unified problem remains open.
